docs.text: Convert JSON, XML, CSV, YAML, BSON and MT940 into any text format with templates. bafi reads structured data from a file or a pipe and renders it through a template into whatever text the next system needs: JSON, XML, CSV, HTML, SQL, a SOAP request. One small program without dependencies for Windows, macOS and Linux. Install · Recipes · Function reference · Troubleshooting · GitHub

docs.text: {"users": [{"name": "Alice", "city": "Prague"}, {"name": "Bob", "city": "Brno"}]} Convert the whole document with one function: bafi -i users.json -t '?{{toYAML .}}' users: - city: Prague name: Alice - city: Brno name: Bob Or describe the output yourself. Text outside {{ }} is copied as it is; range repeats a block for every item: bafi -i users.json -t '?{{range .users}}{{.name}} lives in {{upper .city}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}' Alice lives in PRAGUE Bob lives in BRNO Works in pipes too: curl -fs https://example.com/api/users | bafi -f json -t report.tmpl -o report.html . docs.text: Many inputs: JSON, BSON, YAML, CSV (any delimiter), XML and MT940 bank statements, from a file or standard input. Any output: the template decides. HTML, SQL, shell scripts, SOAP envelopes, fixed-width text. Pipes: read from curl , write to the next command. Bridges REST and SOAP services, databases and spreadsheets. Several inputs at once: merge files of different formats into one output. Helpful errors: problems are reported with the file, line and column, and a hint how to fix them. Extensible: 60+ template functions, plus your own in Lua . TOON and OpenAI: encode data compactly for LLM prompts, or ask OpenAI about your data (experimental). If you like this app you can buy me a coffee ;)

docs.text: Changelog Release notes for bafi. Each release is a level-2 heading ( ## X.Y.Z ) matching version.txt . task release extracts the matching section as the GitHub release body and refuses to tag if the section is missing. Newest release first. 1.5.2 Security toDecimal and toDecimalString reject a number whose exponent is above 10,000, such as "1e99999999" , immediately: toDecimal returns 0 , toDecimalString returns err: ... exceeds MaxDecodeExponent (10000) . Before, one such value in the input could keep bafi busy for minutes while its memory use kept growing. ( shopspring/decimal 1.4.0 → 1.6.0) Minimum Go raised to 1.27.3 ( go.mod ), the release that fixes the stdlib advisory GO-2026-6809 ( crypto/x509 : distrust compromised intermediate certificates; used by the HTTPS connection of -gq ). Release binaries are built with the same version. Changed Lua: file:read on a file that cannot be read, such as a directory, returns nil, message, 1 like standard Lua instead of raising an error. Before, the error ended the Lua function and its place in the output showed luaError: ; now the function carries on, so check what read returns. ( yuin/gopher-lua 1.1.1 → 1.1.2, which also fixes invalid code generated for some consecutive nil assignments and limits recursion in pattern matching.) Updated sashabaranov/go-openai to 1.43.0, and in CI actions/setup-python to 7.1.0 and github/codeql-action to 4.39.1. Fixed toDecimal and toDecimalString accept the Unicode minus sign ( "−5" is -5 ; before it was invalid) and reject a sign after a leading decimal point ( ".-5" was read as a number). 1.5.1 Fixed Comparing values of different types, the classic {{if gt .count 2}} with a JSON number ( float64 against the template's int ) or a CSV text value against a number, now explains the cause and the fix ( 2.0 or (toInt .count) ) instead of a generic hint. Comparing a list or an object, and a comparison with a missing argument, get their own hints too. The function reference shows that add , sub , mul , div , mod , max and min drop decimals ( {{mul "12.50" 2}} is 24 ) and points to the ...f functions for decimal values. 1.5.0 Added Helpful error messages. Errors name the input or template and, where the parser reports it, the line and column; they show the offending line with a caret, explain the likely cause and link to the matching section of the new troubleshooting page. Covers JSON, YAML, XML and CSV input (with location), BSON and MT940 input, template syntax and execution errors, files and flags. Unknown functions and input formats get a "did you mean" suggestion. -strict flag: a key missing from the input stops the run with an error that names the key and the template line, instead of printing <no value> . Warnings on standard error (output unchanged): when the output contains <no value> , and when a CSV header ends up as a single column because of a wrong -d . Task-oriented documentation: 16 recipes (XML to JSON, JSON to CSV, REST to SOAP, HTML reports, SQL from CSV, MT940, ...), install, command line, template guide, function reference, troubleshooting and security pages. The sample commands, the function tables and the error examples in the documentation are executed by the test suite. The online demo is built from this repository on every release and loads only when used. It shows the same error messages as the CLI. Changed Errors are printed without a timestamp and without internal function names. Usage mistakes (no template, no input, unknown flag or -f value, -gk without -gq , a stray argument such as an unquoted inline template) print to standard error and exit with code 2 . Before, some printed to standard output and exited with 0. Runtime errors still exit with 1. A single trailing - (read standard input) is still accepted. With -o , bafi renders the whole result before writing the file: a failing template leaves an existing output file untouched. Before, an error during execution left it half-written. bafi -h shows usage examples and a link to the documentation. Standard input redirected from a file ( bafi -f json ... < data.json ) is accepted; before, only pipes were. The docs build runs in strict mode, so broken internal links fail it. Fixed toXML wrote & , < , > and quotes unescaped, producing invalid XML; for lists it failed with an err: text instead. Files listed in -i '?files.yaml' now have a UTF-8 byte order mark removed, like a single -i file. Some malformed BSON input crashed bafi with a Go stack trace; it is now reported as an input error. Several documentation examples were wrong or depended on APIs that no longer exist. 1.4.0 Security Lua sandbox. The Lua state no longer exposes os.execute , os.exit , os.remove , os.rename , os.tmpname and io.popen . Everything else in the Lua standard library ( os.date , os.time , io.open , require , ...) works as before. If your functions.lua shelled out through one of the removed functions, it will now fail with luaError: ... attempt to call a non-function object . Lazy Lua loading. ./lua/functions.lua is loaded the first time a template calls {{lua ...}} , not at startup. bafi -v , bafi -h and templates that do not use Lua never execute code from the current directory. OpenAI key from the environment. The API key is read from OPENAI_API_KEY when -gk is not given, so it no longer has to appear in process listings and shell history. -gk still works and overrides the variable. CI hardening. All GitHub Actions are pinned by commit SHA, workflows declare minimal permissions , deprecated action versions are upgraded (checkout v7, setup-go v7, setup-python v7, CodeQL v4) and a govulncheck job runs on every push. Dependabot keeps the pins current. Release pipeline rebuilt. Releases are built on the GitHub runner with the Go version from go.mod ( task dist ) instead of the go-release.action Docker image. gofmt/vet, tests and govulncheck gate the release, every asset is listed in a SHA256SUMS.txt , and the release notes are the matching CHANGELOG.md section. go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver bumped to v1.17.10 (GO-2026-5327; the affected GSSAPI code was never reachable from bafi). Minimum Go raised to 1.27.2 ( go.mod ), the release that fixes the stdlib advisories GO-2026-6603 … GO-2026-6617 reported by govulncheck . Release binaries are built with the same version. Release archives: new darwin_arm64 (Apple silicon) and linux_arm64 builds next to the existing windows_amd64 , linux_amd64 , linux_386 and darwin_amd64 . The per-asset MD5 _checksum.txt files are replaced by one SHA256SUMS.txt . task release only tags and pushes; the GitHub release is created by CI. New ## Security notes section in the documentation (trusted templates, no output escaping, CSV formula injection, OpenAI data sharing, randInt ). Added csvSafe template function: prefixes values starting with = , + , - , @ , TAB or CR with ' to defuse spreadsheet formula injection. Plain numbers such as -5 are left untouched. Fixed Lua functions returning a non-string leaked one value on the Lua stack per call. A missing or broken ./lua/functions.lua , or a non-string function name, now yields an inline luaError: in the output instead of aborting the whole run. Unicode CSV delimiters ( -d ) are handled correctly (PR #13). A malformed -i ?files.yaml record (wrong type or missing file / label ) is reported as fileList[<index>]: ... instead of crashing with a stack trace. An invalid hex CSV delimiter ( -d 0xZZ ) is reported as mapCSV: invalid delimiter through the normal error path instead of log.Fatalf . toXML renders []interface{} slices (e.g. from mustArray or nested JSON arrays) as <record> elements instead of failing on a type assertion. randInt cannot overflow on extreme bounds such as {{randInt 0 9223372036854775807}} . An invalid pattern in replaceAllRegex aborts the template with a readable error calling replaceAllRegex: error parsing regexp: ... instead of a recovered panic. An OpenAI response without choices is reported as an error instead of a panic. Changed -gq alone now selects OpenAI mode (key from -gk or OPENAI_API_KEY ). Without any key it fails with OpenAI API key must be defined instead of being silently ignored. format in the -i ?files.yaml file list is optional; it is detected from the file extension when omitted, exactly like for a single -i file. randInt uses math/rand/v2 ; the explicit rand.Seed at startup is gone (the generator is auto-seeded since Go 1.20). Version is read from version.txt (embedded at build time) instead of a constant in main.go . New Taskfile.yml with task build|test|vet|check|vuln|docs|release|clean . task release tags, pushes and publishes the GitHub release that triggers the CI build. The changelog is part of the documentation site. CI release build runs only on published releases (PR #12). 1.3.0 Reconstructed from git history; this release predates the changelog. Added TOON (Token Oriented Object Notation) output via the toTOON template function. Fixed randInt handles an invalid range and includes the upper bound.

docs.text: Command line bafi -i INPUT -t TEMPLATE [-o OUTPUT] COMMAND | bafi -f FORMAT -t TEMPLATE bafi -h prints the same overview with all flags. Flags Flag Meaning -i file Input file. Without -i , bafi reads standard input (a pipe or < file ). -i '?list.yaml' reads several files . -t template Template file, or an inline template starting with ? : -t '?{{toJSON .}}' . -o file Output file. Without -o , the result goes to standard output. -f format Input format: json , bson , yaml , csv , xml , mt940 . Default: from the -i file extension. Required for standard input. -d delimiter CSV delimiter: one character ( -d ';' ) or a hex byte ( -d 0x09 for TAB). Default , . For MT940, the separator between messages. -strict Fail on a key that is missing from the input instead of printing <no value> . -v Print the version. -h Print help. -gq question Ask OpenAI about the input instead of using a template. See Ask OpenAI . -gk key OpenAI API key. Default: the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable (preferred). -gm model OpenAI model: gpt35 (default), gpt4 , gpt4o , gpt4o-mini , gpt5 , gpt5mini , gpt5nano . Flags must come before any other argument. Input bafi -i testdata.xml -t '?{{index .TOP_LEVEL "-description"}}' employeeData The format is taken from the extension: .json , .bson , .yaml / .yml , .csv , .xml (also .cdf , .cdf3 ), .sta (MT940). -f overrides it. Standard input has no name, so -f is required: curl -fs https://example.com/api/users | bafi -f json -t users.tmpl Redirecting a file works the same way: {"users": [{"name": "Alice"}, {"name": "Bob"}]} bafi -f json -t '?{{len .users}} users' < users.json 2 users A single - after the flags, the usual "read standard input" marker, is accepted and changes nothing. A UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the input is ignored. Several input files -i '?list.yaml' reads every file named in a YAML list and makes each available under its label (quote it: zsh, the macOS default shell, treats an unquoted ? as a wildcard): - file: rates.xml label: RATES # {{ .RATES }} - file: orders.json label: ORDERS format: json # optional; the extension decides when omitted -f is ignored in this mode; -d applies to every CSV file. Full example: Merge several files into one output . Templates on the command line An inline template starts with ? . Quote it so the shell passes it as one argument: Shell Example bash, zsh bafi -i data.json -t '?{{toXML .}}' PowerShell .\bafi.exe -i data.json -t "?{{toXML .}}" cmd.exe bafi.exe -i data.json -t "?{{toXML .}}" Inside single quotes, template strings use double quotes: -t '?{{index . "my-key"}}' . A template file avoids quoting issues altogether: -t report.tmpl . The template guide explains the syntax. Output The result goes to standard output unless -o names a file. bafi renders the whole result first: when a template fails, standard output stays empty and an existing -o file is left as it was, so a pipe never receives half a document and a scheduled job keeps its last good report. Append to a file with the shell: bafi -i testdata.xml -t template.tmpl >> output.txt Errors, warnings and exit codes Errors and warnings go to standard error, never into the output. An error names the file and line, shows the problem and suggests a fix; see Troubleshooting . Exit code Meaning 0 Success (warnings may have been printed). 1 The input, the template, the output file or the OpenAI request failed. 2 The command line is wrong: missing template or input, unknown flag or format. Warnings do not change the output or the exit code: the output contains <no value> because the template used a key the input does not have; a CSV header ended up as a single column, which usually means the wrong -d . Strict mode -strict turns a missing key into an error with the key name and the template line, instead of printing <no value> : bafi -i testdata.xml -strict -t '?{{.TOP_LEVEL.DATA_LINES}}' bafi: template error in the inline template (line 1, column 3) 1 | {{.TOP_LEVEL.DATA_LINES}} | ^ map has no entry for key "DATA_LINES" (at <.TOP_LEVEL.DATA_LINES>) hint: the input has no key "DATA_LINES" here (-strict is on); check spelling and case - XML attributes start with "-" (index . "-id"); for keys that may be absent use {{with index . "DATA_LINES"}}...{{end}} docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#missing-keys-and-no-value Use it while writing a template, and in automation where a missing field must not go unnoticed. For keys that may legitimately be absent, use index : {{with index . "nickname"}}{{.}}{{end}} .

Values from JSON, YAML, XML and CSV are converted automatically where it makes sense, so {{add "1" 2}} works too. Every example on this page is executed by the test suite; the result column is what bafi prints. Rows marked * change on every run. Math functions Function Example Result add - sum of integers {{add 1 2 "3"}} 6 add1 - plus one {{add1 41}} 42 sub - subtract {{sub 10 4}} 6 mul - product of integers {{mul 2 3 4}} 24 div - integer division {{div 7 2}} 3 mod - remainder {{mod 7 2}} 1 addf - exact decimal sum {{addf 0.1 0.2}} 0.3 add1f - plus one, decimal {{add1f 1.5}} 2.5 subf - decimal subtract {{subf 1.5 0.2 0.3}} 1 mulf - decimal product {{mulf 1.1 3}} 3.3 divf - decimal division {{divf 10 4}} 2.5 round - to N decimals {{round 3.14159 2}} 3.14 round - custom rounding point {{round 6.35 1 0.4}} 6.4 max - largest integer {{max 3 9 "5"}} 9 min - smallest integer {{min 3 9 "5"}} 3 maxf - largest number {{maxf 1.5 2.25}} 2.25 minf - smallest number {{minf 1.5 2.25}} 1.5 randInt - random integer, both bounds included {{randInt 1 6}} * mul on a decimal value - the decimals are dropped {{mul "12.50" 2}} 24 mulf on the same value {{mulf "12.50" 2}} 25 add , add1 , sub , mul , div , mod , max and min work with whole numbers and silently drop decimals, as the mul row shows; use them for counts and IDs. docs.text: Install bafi is a single program without dependencies. Download it, unpack it, run it. Download Get the archive for your system from the latest release : System Archive Windows (64-bit) bafi_vX.Y.Z_windows_amd64.zip macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and newer) bafi_vX.Y.Z_darwin_arm64.tgz macOS, Intel bafi_vX.Y.Z_darwin_amd64.tgz Linux, x86-64 bafi_vX.Y.Z_linux_amd64.tgz Linux, ARM 64-bit (Raspberry Pi 4/5, Graviton) bafi_vX.Y.Z_linux_arm64.tgz Linux, 32-bit x86 bafi_vX.Y.Z_linux_386.tgz Each archive contains the bafi program, this documentation, the sample testdata.xml and template.tmpl , and the example Lua functions in lua/ . Verify the download SHA256SUMS.txt in the release lists the checksum of every archive: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing # Linux shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing # macOS On Windows: Get-FileHash .\bafi_vX.Y.Z_windows_amd64.zip and compare with the line in SHA256SUMS.txt . Unpack and run Linux tar xzf bafi_vX.Y.Z_linux_amd64.tgz ./bafi -v sudo mv bafi /usr/local/bin/ # optional: run it from anywhere macOS tar xzf bafi_vX.Y.Z_darwin_arm64.tgz xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./bafi # only needed when the archive was downloaded with a browser ./bafi -v macOS refuses to open programs downloaded with a browser unless an Apple-registered developer signed them; removing the quarantine flag once fixes that. Windows Unzip the archive, open PowerShell in that folder and run: .\bafi.exe -v PowerShell needs the .\ prefix for programs in the current folder. To run bafi from anywhere, move bafi.exe to a folder listed in the PATH environment variable. SmartScreen may warn the first time: choose More info , then Run anyway . With Go If you have Go 1.27.3 or newer: go install github.com/mmalcek/bafi@latest The program lands in $(go env GOPATH)/bin . First steps bafi -i testdata.xml -t template.tmpl Then pick a task from the recipes .

docs.text: Security notes bafi is a local formatter: whoever controls the template controls the output. Keep these points in mind when you use it in automation. Templates and Lua are trusted code A template can call every built-in function and every Lua function, so never run templates or a lua/ directory from an untrusted source. Only the input is treated as data: values in the input can never inject template actions. ./lua/functions.lua is loaded from the current working directory the first time a template calls lua , and runs with the permissions of the bafi process. Functions that start programs, end bafi or delete and rename files are removed ( os.execute , os.exit , os.remove , os.rename , os.tmpname , io.popen ); the rest of the Lua standard library ( os.date , os.time , io.open , require , ...) works normally. bafi -v , bafi -h and templates that do not call lua never execute Lua code. No output escaping bafi uses Go's text/template , which writes values verbatim. If the output is HTML, XML, SQL, a shell script or JSON, a value containing quotes, < or ; goes straight through. Use toJSON , toXML , toYAML or toTOON to produce structured output from data instead of building it from strings, use html for HTML and XML text, and escape values yourself for other formats (see Template guide ). CSV formula injection Spreadsheet software evaluates cells that start with = , + , - , @ , TAB or CR. When CSV output will be opened in Excel or LibreOffice and the input is not under your control, wrap values with csvSafe (see JSON to CSV ). OpenAI mode sends your data away With -gq , the question and the entire parsed input are sent to OpenAI. Pass the key through the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable rather than -gk , so it does not appear in process listings and shell history. randInt is not a secure random source Use uuid (backed by crypto/rand ) for identifiers; never derive tokens or passwords from randInt . Verbose error messages Errors include file paths and an excerpt of the input or template to make problems easy to fix. Keep that in mind if standard error ends up in shared logs. Verifying downloads Every release lists the SHA-256 checksum of each archive in SHA256SUMS.txt ; see Install .

docs.text: Template guide bafi templates are Go text/template templates: plain text with actions in {{ }} . Everything outside the braces is copied to the output as it is. The examples below use this input: { "company": "Example Ltd", "users": [ {"name": "Alice", "age": 34, "roles": ["admin", "dev"], "my-id": "A1"}, {"name": "Bob", "age": 19, "roles": ["dev"], "my-id": "B2"} ] } In VS Code the gotemplate-syntax extension adds highlighting. Accessing data The dot . is the current data; at the start it is the whole input. Follow keys with more dots: bafi -i users.json -t '?{{.company}} has {{len .users}} users' Example Ltd has 2 users {{index .users 0}} - an item of a list (counting from 0). {{index . "my-id"}} - keys containing - , spaces or other special characters need index . {{toJSON .users}} - print any part of the data, which is the quickest way to find a path. $ is always the root, even inside range or with : {{$.company}} . docs.text: Troubleshooting Every bafi error names the file, the line and usually the column, shows the offending line, and ends with a hint and a link to the matching section below. The examples on this page are real output of the current version. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 the input, template or output failed, 2 the command line is wrong. Command line No input bafi -t '?{{toJSON .}}' bafi: no input hint: read a file with -i data.json, or pipe data in: cat data.json | bafi -f json -t '?{{toXML .}}' docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#no-input usage: bafi -i INPUT -t TEMPLATE [-o OUTPUT] (bafi -h for help and examples) Without -i , bafi reads standard input, and nothing was piped in. Give a file with -i data.json , or pipe data: cat data.json | bafi -f json -t ... . Redirecting works as well: bafi -f json -t ... < data.json . Unexpected argument The shell splits an inline template at spaces unless it is quoted: {"name": "Alice", "count": 3} bafi -i data.json -t ?{{toJSON .}} bafi: unexpected argument ".}}" hint: flags must come first and inline templates with spaces must be quoted: -t '?{{toJSON .}}' docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#unexpected-argument usage: bafi -i INPUT -t TEMPLATE [-o OUTPUT] (bafi -h for help and examples) Quote inline templates: single quotes in bash/zsh ( -t '?{{toJSON .}}' ), double quotes in PowerShell and cmd.exe ( -t "?{{toJSON .}}" ). All flags must come before any other argument. The output above is from bash; zsh, the macOS default shell, stops even earlier with zsh: no matches found , because it treats the unquoted ? as a wildcard. The fix is the same: quote the template. Unknown input format echo '{"a": 1}' | bafi -t '?{{.a}}' bafi: cannot tell the input format of stdin hint: add -f json (the input looks like JSON); supported formats: json, bson, yaml, csv, xml, mt940 docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#unknown-input-format usage: bafi -i INPUT -t TEMPLATE [-o OUTPUT] (bafi -h for help and examples) Standard input has no file name, so bafi cannot guess the format: add -f json , -f xml , -f csv , -f yaml , -f bson or -f mt940 . For files, the extension decides ( .json , .xml , .csv , .yaml / .yml , .bson , .sta ); -f overrides it. A misspelled -f value gets a suggestion. File not found bafi -i data.jsn -t '?{{.name}}' bafi: cannot read input file "data.jsn" no such file or directory hint: check the path; relative paths are resolved from the current directory docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#file-not-found Relative paths start in the current directory, not where bafi is installed. The same error for -t usually means the inline template is missing its leading ? . Cannot create output file bafi -i data.json -t '?{{.name}}' -o reports/today.txt bafi: cannot create output file "reports/today.txt" no such file or directory hint: the directory does not exist; create it first docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#cannot-create-output-file bafi does not create directories; create reports first. Input data Input is empty echo '' | bafi -f json -t '?{{.name}}' bafi: JSON input from stdin is empty hint: nothing arrived on stdin - did the previous command in the pipe fail? (with curl use -f so HTTP errors are reported) docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#input-is-empty Usually the command before bafi failed and printed its error to the terminal instead of the pipe. With curl, add -f so HTTP errors are reported, and -s to hide the progress bar: curl -fs URL | bafi ... . Invalid JSON { "name": "Alice", "tags": ["a", "b",], } bafi -i broken.json -t '?{{.name}}' bafi: cannot parse JSON input from "broken.json" (line 3, column 21) 3 | "tags": ["a", "b",], | ^ invalid character ']' looking for beginning of value hint: remove the trailing comma before ] - JSON does not allow it docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#invalid-json The most common causes: a trailing comma, single quotes instead of double quotes, keys or text values without quotes, or a file cut off in the middle. bafi expects an object {...} or a list of objects [{...}, ...] at the top level. Invalid YAML name: Alice role: admin bafi -i broken.yaml -t '?{{.name}}' bafi: cannot parse YAML input from "broken.yaml" (near line 2) 1 | name: Alice 2 | role: admin mapping values are not allowed in this context hint: check the indentation; a value containing ": " must be quoted, e.g. title: "Note: read me" docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#invalid-yaml YAML reports problems at or just before the line where it got confused, so check the line above as well. Indent with spaces only; quote values that contain : or start with special characters. Invalid XML <order> <customer>Tom & Jerry</customer> </order> bafi -i broken.xml -t '?{{.order.customer}}' bafi: cannot parse XML input from "broken.xml" (line 2, column 17) 2 | <customer>Tom & Jerry</customer> | ^ XML syntax error on line 2: invalid character entity & (no semicolon) hint: a bare & must be written as & (and < as <) inside XML text docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#invalid-xml Inside XML text & must be written & and < must be < . Other frequent causes are a closing tag that does not match ( <b>...</c> ) and a document that was cut off. Only UTF-8 XML is supported. Invalid CSV name,comment Alice,said "hi" bafi -i quotes.csv -t '?{{len .}}' bafi: cannot parse CSV input from "quotes.csv" (line 2, column 12) 2 | Alice,said "hi" | ^ bare " in non-quoted-field hint: a quote inside an unquoted field: quote the whole field and double the inner quotes, e.g. "He said ""hi""" docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#invalid-csv A field that contains quotes must itself be quoted, with the inner quotes doubled: Alice,"said ""hi""" . CSV: wrong number of fields name,city Alice,Prague Bob,Brno,CZ bafi -i fields.csv -t '?{{len .}}' bafi: cannot parse CSV input from "fields.csv" (line 3) 3 | Bob,Brno,CZ wrong number of fields: the header has 2, this record has 3 hint: every row needs as many fields as the header; quote values that contain the delimiter ("Smith, John"), or set the delimiter with -d docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#csv-wrong-number-of-fields Every row needs as many values as the header line. Values containing the delimiter must be quoted ( "Brno, CZ" ). CSV in one column name;city Alice;Prague bafi -i semicolon.csv -t '?{{range .}}{{.name}}{{end}}' bafi: warning: the CSV header has a single column containing ';' - did you mean -d ';'? bafi: warning: output contains <no value> 1 time(s) - a key used in the template is missing from the input (or is null); run with -strict to see which one The file uses ; , but bafi split at commas, so the whole line became one column named name;city . Set the delimiter: -d ';' , or -d 0x09 for TAB-separated files. Invalid file list - file: data.json label: DATA - file: 42 label: OTHER bafi -i '?files.yaml' -t '?{{toJSON .}}' bafi: invalid entry in file list "files.yaml" fileList[1]: "file" must be a string (got int) hint: every entry needs file and label as text, format is optional: - file: rates.xml / label: RATES docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#invalid-file-list Each entry of a file list needs file and label as text; format is optional when the extension is known. Invalid input Errors in BSON and MT940 input have no line numbers. this is not a SWIFT message bafi -i statement.sta -t '?{{.Fields.F_20}}' bafi: cannot parse MT940 input from "statement.sta" no {1: header block found (headerStartNotFound) hint: an MT940 message starts with the {1:...}{2:...}{4: header, uses CRLF line endings and ends with -}; for files with several messages (e.g. Multicash) set the separator, e.g. -d "-}\r\n" docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#invalid-input MT940 files need the {1:...}{2:...}{4: header, CRLF line endings and -} at the end. BSON input must be a BSON document or a mongodump file; MongoDB extended JSON is JSON ( -f json ). Templates Template syntax error Users: {{range .users}} - {{.name}} bafi -i data.json -t report.tmpl bafi: template error in report.tmpl (line 2) 2 | {{range .users}} unexpected EOF: the {{range}} started here has no {{end}} hint: a {{if}}, {{range}} or {{with}} block is missing its {{end}} docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#template-syntax-error Every {{if}} , {{range}} and {{with}} needs its {{end}} , and every {{ needs }} . Unknown function bafi -i data.json -t '?{{uper .name}}' bafi: template error in the inline template (line 1) 1 | {{uper .name}} function "uper" not defined hint: there is no function "uper" - did you mean "upper"? docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#unknown-function Function names are case-sensitive. See the function reference . Keys with dashes {"order-id": 1001} bafi -i dashes.json -t '?{{.order-id}}' bafi: template error in the inline template (line 1) 1 | {{.order-id}} bad character U+002D '-' hint: keys containing "-" cannot be used with a dot; use index: {{index . "my-key"}} (XML attributes are "-name") docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#keys-with-dashes A dot path cannot contain - (or spaces). Use index , which also reaches XML attributes, because those are stored with a leading - : bafi -i dashes.json -t '?{{index . "order-id"}}' 1001 Wrong type bafi -i data.json -t '?{{upper .count}}' bafi: template error in the inline template (line 1, column 9) 1 | {{upper .count}} | ^ wrong type for value; expected string; got float64 (at <.count>) hint: the value is a float64, the function needs text; convert it first, e.g. (toString .value) docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#wrong-type JSON numbers are numbers ( float64 ), while CSV and XML values are always text. Convert where the function expects something else: {{upper (toString .count)}} , {{add (toInt .qty) 1}} . range needs a list: an XML element that occurs once is not a list, wrap it with mustArray . The same applies to comparisons, where it is easy to miss: a number written in the template is an integer, a JSON or YAML number is a float64 , and the two cannot be compared directly. bafi -i data.json -t '?{{if gt .count 2}}many{{end}}' bafi: template error in the inline template (line 1, column 6) 1 | {{if gt .count 2}}many{{end}} | ^ error calling gt: incompatible types for comparison: float64 and int (at <gt .count 2>) hint: numbers from JSON and YAML are float64, numbers written in the template are int; write the number with a decimal point (2.0) or convert the value: (toInt .count) docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#wrong-type Write the number with a decimal point, or convert the value: bafi -i data.json -t '?{{if gt .count 2.0}}many{{end}} / {{if gt (toInt .count) 2}}many{{end}}' many / many Missing keys and <no value> A key that is not in the input prints <no value> . bafi keeps the output but warns: bafi -i data.json -t '?Hello {{.nmae}}' bafi: warning: output contains <no value> 1 time(s) - a key used in the template is missing from the input (or is null); run with -strict to see which one -strict turns it into an error that names the key and the line: bafi -i data.json -strict -t '?Hello {{.nmae}}' bafi: template error in the inline template (line 1, column 9) 1 | Hello {{.nmae}} | ^ map has no entry for key "nmae" (at <.nmae>) hint: the input has no key "nmae" here (-strict is on); check spelling and case - XML attributes start with "-" (index . "-id"); for keys that may be absent use {{with index . "nmae"}}...{{end}} docs: https://mmalcek.github.io/bafi/troubleshooting/#missing-keys-and-no-value Check spelling and case ( Name and name are different keys); XML attributes start with - . To see what bafi parsed, print it: bafi -i data.json -t '?{{toJSON .}}' . Under -strict , keys that may legitimately be absent need index , which returns nothing instead of failing: {{with index . "nickname"}}({{.}}){{end}} . Installation macOS: bafi cannot be opened macOS blocks programs downloaded with a browser that are not signed by an Apple developer ("cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified"). Remove the quarantine flag once: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./bafi Files downloaded with curl are not quarantined. See Install . PowerShell: bafi is not recognized PowerShell does not run programs from the current directory by name. Use .\bafi.exe , or put bafi in a directory listed in PATH . Windows SmartScreen may warn the first time; choose More info , then Run anyway . Lua errors in the output Lua problems do not stop bafi; the output contains luaError: ... where the function's result should be. See Custom logic with Lua .

docs.text: Convert a MongoDB dump (BSON) to CSV Read .bson files written by mongodump (or a single BSON document) and turn them into CSV, JSON or any other text, without a running MongoDB. mongodump --db shop --collection users --out dump bafi -i dump/shop/users.bson -t users-csv.tmpl -o users.csv A mongodump file holds one document per record; bafi reads it as a list, so the template iterates with range . . A file with a single document is read as that document. Try it without MongoDB Make a small BSON file from JSON with toBSON , then read it back: {"name": "Alice Smith", "email": "alice@example.com", "roles": ["admin", "billing"]} bafi -i user.json -t '?{{toBSON .}}' -o user.bson name,email,roles "{{.name}}",{{.email}},"{{range $i, $r := .roles}}{{if $i}};{{end}}{{$r}}{{end}}" bafi -i user.bson -t user-csv.tmpl name,email,roles "Alice Smith",alice@example.com,"admin;billing" For a dump with many users, wrap the data line in {{range .}}...{{end}} . Inspect a dump When you do not know the structure of a collection, print the first record: bafi -i dump/shop/users.bson -t '?{{toJSON (index . 0)}}' MongoDB's own types (ObjectId, dates) are printed in their Go form; convert them in the template or with toString . docs.text: Convert between JSON, YAML, TOON and BSON Generic format conversion needs no template file: an inline template with one conversion function is enough. The input format comes from the file extension or from -f . Sample input service: billing replicas: 3 ports: - 8080 - 8443 owner: team: payments email: payments@example.com YAML to JSON bafi -i config.yaml -t '?{{toJSON .}}' { "owner": { "email": "payments@example.com", "team": "payments" }, "ports": [ 8080, 8443 ], "replicas": 3, "service": "billing" } JSON to YAML {"service": "billing", "replicas": 3, "ports": [8080, 8443]} bafi -i config.json -t '?{{toYAML .}}' ports: - 8080 - 8443 replicas: 3 service: billing To TOON (for LLM prompts) TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) carries the same data as JSON with far fewer tokens, which makes prompts to language models cheaper. bafi -i config.yaml -t '?{{toTOON .}}' owner: email: payments@example.com team: payments ports[2]: 8080,8443 replicas: 3 service: billing To BSON (MongoDB) toBSON writes binary BSON, so send it to a file rather than the terminal: bafi -i config.json -t '?{{toBSON .}}' -o config.bson …and read it back like any other input: bafi -i config.bson -t '?{{.service}} runs {{.replicas}} replicas' billing runs 3 replicas Notes Keys are sorted alphabetically in JSON and YAML output; JSON and YAML maps have no order. toJSON indents with two spaces. To control the layout or the value types, write the JSON in the template as in CSV to JSON . In PowerShell use double quotes around inline templates: .\bafi.exe -i config.yaml -t "?{{toJSON .}}" . Related: XML to JSON · JSON to XML

docs.text: Convert CSV to JSON Turn a CSV file (an export from Excel, a database or another tool) into JSON. Each row becomes an object whose keys are the column names from the header line. Sample input id,name,email,active 1,Alice Smith,alice@example.com,true 2,"Brown, Bob",bob@example.com,false Values that contain the delimiter are quoted ( "Brown, Bob" ); that is standard CSV ( RFC 4180 ). One-line conversion bafi -i users.csv -t '?{{toJSON .}}' [ { "active": "true", "email": "alice@example.com", "id": "1", "name": "Alice Smith" }, { "active": "false", "email": "bob@example.com", "id": "2", "name": "Brown, Bob" } ] Every CSV value is text, so the generic conversion produces strings only. Numbers and booleans Write the JSON yourself to choose the types. toJSON quotes and escapes text values: [ {{- range $i, $u := .}}{{if $i}},{{end}} {"id": {{$u.id}}, "name": {{toJSON $u.name}}, "active": {{$u.active}}} {{- end}} ] bafi -i users.csv -t users-json.tmpl [ {"id": 1, "name": "Alice Smith", "active": true}, {"id": 2, "name": "Brown, Bob", "active": false} ] Semicolons, tabs and other delimiters Many European exports use ; . Set the delimiter with -d : any single character, or a hex byte such as 0x09 for TAB. id;name 1;Alice Smith bafi -i export.csv -d ';' -t '?{{toJSON .}}' [ { "id": "1", "name": "Alice Smith" } ] If you forget -d , bafi warns that the whole header ended up in a single column. Related: JSON to CSV · SQL INSERT statements from CSV

docs.text: Generate SQL INSERT statements from CSV Load a CSV export into a database without an import wizard: generate INSERT statements and run them with your usual SQL client. Sample input sku,name,price A-1,Coffee beans,12.90 B-7,O'Reilly mug,9.50 Template Text values go in single quotes, so a quote inside a value must be doubled: O'Reilly becomes 'O''Reilly' . replaceAll "'" "''" does exactly that. INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price) VALUES {{- range $i, $p := .}}{{if $i}},{{end}} ('{{replaceAll "'" "''" $p.sku}}', '{{replaceAll "'" "''" $p.name}}', {{toFloat64 $p.price}}) {{- end}}; bafi -i products.csv -t insert.tmpl INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price) VALUES ('A-1', 'Coffee beans', 12.9), ('B-7', 'O''Reilly mug', 9.5); toFloat64 makes sure the price is a number; a malformed value becomes 0 instead of breaking the SQL. Pipe the result straight into the client, for example bafi -i products.csv -t insert.tmpl | psql shop or | sqlite3 shop.db . Note: escaping quotes is enough for trusted exports. For data from untrusted sources prefer your database's bulk loader ( COPY , LOAD DATA , bcp ) with the CSV itself. Related: CSV to JSON · Query a SQL database into XML or JSON

docs.text: Convert JSON to CSV Turn JSON, typically a list of objects from an API, into a CSV file that opens cleanly in Excel or LibreOffice. Sample input { "users": [ {"id": 1, "name": "Alice Smith", "email": "alice@example.com"}, {"id": 2, "name": "Brown, Bob", "email": "bob@example.com"}, {"id": 3, "name": "=HYPERLINK(\"http://evil.example\")", "email": "x@example.com"} ] } Template The header is a plain line; range writes one line per user. {{- trims the line break before it, so no empty lines appear. id,name,email {{- range .users}} {{.id}},"{{replaceAll "\"" "\"\"" (csvSafe .name)}}",{{.email}} {{- end}} bafi -i users.json -t users-csv.tmpl id,name,email 1,"Alice Smith",alice@example.com 2,"Brown, Bob",bob@example.com 3,"'=HYPERLINK(""http://evil.example"")",x@example.com What the template takes care of: Commas inside values : the name is wrapped in quotes, and quotes inside it are doubled ( replaceAll "\"" "\"\"" ), as CSV requires. Formula injection : csvSafe prefixes values starting with = , + , - , @ with ' , so a spreadsheet shows them as text instead of executing them. Plain numbers such as -5 are left alone. Use it whenever the data comes from outside. Write to a file bafi -i users.json -t users-csv.tmpl -o users.csv From an API: curl -fs https://example.com/api/users | bafi -f json -t users-csv.tmpl -o users.csv Related: CSV to JSON · XML to CSV

docs.text: Convert JSON to XML Turn JSON, for example a REST API response, into XML: generic XML in one line, or the exact XML layout another system expects. Sample input { "users": [ {"id": 1, "name": "Alice Smith", "email": "alice@example.com"}, {"id": 2, "name": "Tom & Jerry", "email": "tj@example.com"} ] } One-line conversion bafi -i users.json -t '?{{toXML .}}' <doc> <users> <email>alice@example.com</email> <id>1</id> <name>Alice Smith</name> </users> <users> <email>tj@example.com</email> <id>2</id> <name>Tom & Jerry</name> </users> </doc> toXML wraps everything in <doc> ; a top-level JSON array becomes a list of <record> elements. Special characters such as & are escaped for you. Your own XML layout When the receiving system expects specific element names, write them in the template. Use the built-in html function on every value: it escapes & , < , > and quotes, which is exactly what XML text and attributes need. <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <Customers> {{- range .users}} <Customer id="{{.id}}"> <Name>{{html .name}}</Name> <Email>{{html .email}}</Email> </Customer> {{- end}} </Customers> bafi -i users.json -t users-xml.tmpl <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <Customers> <Customer id="1"> <Name>Alice Smith</Name> <Email>alice@example.com</Email> </Customer> <Customer id="2"> <Name>Tom & Jerry</Name> <Email>tj@example.com</Email> </Customer> </Customers> JSON numbers are printed without decimals when they are whole ( 1 , not 1.0 ). From an API curl -fs https://example.com/api/users | bafi -f json -t users-xml.tmpl -o customers.xml Related: XML to JSON · REST response to SOAP request

docs.text: Custom logic with Lua When template functions are not enough - parsing a complex field, a checksum, a lookup table - write the logic in Lua and call it from the template. 1. Write the function bafi loads ./lua/functions.lua from the current directory the first time a template calls lua . Every function receives its arguments as one JSON-encoded array and must return a string. The json.lua helper that ships with bafi decodes the arguments: json = require './lua/json' -- IBAN check: move the first 4 characters to the end, letters to numbers, mod 97 must be 1 function ibanValid(incomingData) local iban = string.upper(string.gsub(json.decode(incomingData)[1], "%s", "")) local moved = string.sub(iban, 5) .. string.sub(iban, 1, 4) local digits = string.gsub(moved, "%a", function(c) return tostring(string.byte(c) - 55) end) local remainder = 0 for i = 1, #digits do remainder = (remainder * 10 + tonumber(string.sub(digits, i, i))) % 97 end return tostring(remainder == 1) end lua/json.lua must sit next to it (it is included in every release archive). 2. Call it from a template owner,iban Alice,CZ65 0800 0000 1920 0014 5399 Bob,CZ65 0800 0000 1920 0014 5398 bafi -i accounts.csv -t '?{{range .}}{{.owner}}: {{lua "ibanValid" .iban}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}' Alice: true Bob: false Arguments are passed as {{lua "functionName" arg1 arg2 ...}} ; in Lua, json.decode(incomingData)[1] is the first one (Lua lists start at 1). Errors Problems inside Lua do not stop the template; the function's place in the output shows the message instead, for example luaError: ... attempt to call a non-function object for a misspelled function name. Search the output for luaError when something looks wrong. Library calls that report failure through their return value, such as io.open and file:read , give back nil and a message as in standard Lua and produce no luaError ; check what they return. Security ./lua/functions.lua is code, and it runs with your permissions. Only use a lua/ directory you trust. bafi removes the functions that start programs or delete files ( os.execute , io.popen , os.remove , ...); the rest of the Lua standard library works. More in Security notes . The shipped example defines sum and mul : {{lua "sum" .val1 .val2}} . Related: MT940 bank statement to CSV · Function reference

docs.text: Merge several files into one output Combine data from several files, even in different formats, into a single report: exchange rates from an XML feed plus orders from a JSON export, for example. 1. List the input files A small YAML file names every input and the label it gets in the template: - file: rates.xml # path, relative to the current directory label: RATES # the data is available as {{ .RATES }} - file: orders.json label: ORDERS # format omitted: taken from the .json extension # format: json # set it when the extension is missing or unusual Pass it with a ? in front of the name, in quotes: -i '?files.yaml' . Without quotes, zsh (the macOS default shell) treats ? as a wildcard and stops with no matches found . 2. The input files <rates date="2024-03-01"> <rate currency="USD">1.0812</rate> <rate currency="CZK">25.304</rate> </rates> [ {"id": 1, "amount": 100, "currency": "USD"}, {"id": 2, "amount": 2530, "currency": "CZK"} ] 3. Template Labels are the top-level keys. $ always refers to the root, which is handy inside range . Orders in EUR (rates of {{index .RATES.rates "-date"}}) {{- range .ORDERS}} {{- $order := .}} {{- range $.RATES.rates.rate}} {{- if eq (index . "-currency") $order.currency}} #{{$order.id}}: {{$order.amount}} {{$order.currency}} = {{round (divf $order.amount (index . "#text")) 2}} EUR {{- end}} {{- end}} {{- end}} bafi -i '?files.yaml' -t summary.tmpl Orders in EUR (rates of 2024-03-01) #1: 100 USD = 92.49 EUR #2: 2530 CZK = 99.98 EUR In PowerShell and cmd.exe use double quotes: -i "?files.yaml" . Each file is parsed on its own, so a broken file is reported with its own name and line. The -d delimiter applies to every CSV file in the list. Related: HTML report from JSON · Command line

docs.text: Convert an MT940 bank statement to CSV Turn a SWIFT MT940 statement ( .sta ) into CSV for accounting software or a spreadsheet. What the parsed statement looks like bafi splits the message into fields named after their tags, prefixed with F_ : .Header - the header blocks {1:...}{2:...} .Fields - statement-level fields: :20: is .Fields.F_20 , :60F: is .Fields.F_60F , ... .Transactions - one entry per :61: line, with its :86: details: .F_61 , .F_86 The values are the raw field texts; split them in the template (or in Lua ). Sample statement {1:F01BANKCZPPAXXX0000000000}{2:I940BANKCZPPXXXXN}{4: :20:STMT-2024-001 :25:CZ6508000000192000145399 :28C:1/1 :60F:C240301EUR1000,00 :61:2403040304C250,00NTRFNONREF :86:Invoice 2024-17 paid by Alice Smith :61:2403050305D99,90NTRFNONREF :86:Office supplies :62F:C240305EUR1150,10 -} Template slice cuts fixed positions out of :61: (date YYMMDD , then C / D ), and dateFormat turns the date into DD.MM.YYYY . Statement,Date,Type,Details {{- $ref := .Fields.F_20}} {{- range .Transactions}} {{$ref}},{{dateFormat (slice .F_61 0 6) "060102" "02.01.2006"}},{{if eq (slice .F_61 10 11) "C"}}credit{{else}}debit{{end}},"{{.F_86}}" {{- end}} bafi -i statement.sta -t statement-csv.tmpl Statement,Date,Type,Details STMT-2024-001,04.03.2024,credit,"Invoice 2024-17 paid by Alice Smith" STMT-2024-001,05.03.2024,debit,"Office supplies" .sta files are recognised by their extension; for other names add -f mt940 . Several statements in one file Exports such as Multicash put many messages in one file. Pass the separator between messages with -d ; bafi then returns a list of statements: bafi -i multicash.sta -d "-}\r\n" -t '?{{range .}}{{.Fields.F_20}} {{end}}' \r and \n in -d are turned into real line breaks. Related: Custom logic with Lua · Template guide

docs.text: Ask OpenAI about your data Instead of writing a template, describe the result in plain language and let an OpenAI model produce it: a summary, an answer, or a conversion that is hard to express as a template. Experimental. export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... curl -fs https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-daily.xml \ | bafi -f xml -gq "What is the current CZK rate? Answer with the number only." -gq is the question; it switches bafi into OpenAI mode, no -t needed. The key comes from the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable. -gk also works but puts the key in your shell history and the process list. -gm picks the model: gpt35 (default), gpt4 , gpt4o , gpt4o-mini , gpt5 , gpt5mini , gpt5nano . -o answer.txt saves the answer to a file. What is sent bafi sends the question and the whole parsed input , encoded as TOON to save tokens. Do not use it with data that must not leave your network. Preview exactly what goes out: {"invoice": "2024-17", "customer": "Alice Smith", "lines": [{"item": "Coffee", "qty": 2, "price": 12.9}]} bafi -i invoice.json -t '?{{toTOON .}}' customer: Alice Smith invoice: 2024-17 lines[1]{item,price,qty}: Coffee,12.9,2 Examples bafi -i invoice.json -gq "Create a UBL 2.1 XML invoice from this data" -gm gpt4o -o invoice.xml curl -fs "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=50.08&longitude=14.42&hourly=temperature_2m" \ | bafi -f json -gm gpt4o-mini -gq "Summarise tomorrow's temperatures in two sentences" Model output is not deterministic; for repeatable conversions write a template instead and keep OpenAI for exploration. Related: Convert between JSON, YAML, TOON and BSON · Security notes

docs.text: Turn a REST (JSON) response into a SOAP request Bridge a REST service and a SOAP service in one pipe: fetch JSON, render the SOAP envelope the other side expects, and post it. curl -fs https://shop.example.com/api/orders/1001 \ | bafi -f json -t create-invoice.tmpl \ | curl -fs -H 'Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8' -H 'SOAPAction: "CreateInvoice"' \ --data-binary @- https://erp.example.com/InvoiceService The JSON coming from REST { "id": 1001, "customer": {"name": "Alice & Co.", "vat": "CZ12345678"}, "items": [ {"sku": "A-1", "qty": 2, "price": 10.5}, {"sku": "B-7", "qty": 1, "price": 99} ] } The SOAP template Every text value goes through html , which escapes & , < , > and quotes, so the envelope stays valid XML whatever the data contains. mulf multiplies decimals exactly (no 20.999999 surprises). <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:inv="http://erp.example.com/invoice"> <soap:Body> <inv:CreateInvoice> <inv:OrderId>{{.id}}</inv:OrderId> <inv:Customer vat="{{html .customer.vat}}">{{html .customer.name}}</inv:Customer> {{- range .items}} <inv:Line sku="{{html .sku}}" quantity="{{.qty}}" amount="{{mulf .qty .price}}"/> {{- end}} </inv:CreateInvoice> </soap:Body> </soap:Envelope> Try it locally cat order.json | bafi -f json -t create-invoice.tmpl <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:inv="http://erp.example.com/invoice"> <soap:Body> <inv:CreateInvoice> <inv:OrderId>1001</inv:OrderId> <inv:Customer vat="CZ12345678">Alice & Co.</inv:Customer> <inv:Line sku="A-1" quantity="2" amount="21"/> <inv:Line sku="B-7" quantity="1" amount="99"/> </inv:CreateInvoice> </soap:Body> </soap:Envelope> Check the request before sending it: run the first two commands of the pipe and read the output, or save it with -o request.xml . Related: SOAP response to JSON · JSON to XML

docs.text: Turn a SOAP response into JSON Call a SOAP service and hand a clean JSON document to a REST client, a script or a web page. curl -fs -H 'Content-Type: text/xml' --data-binary @get-order.xml https://erp.example.com/OrderService \ | bafi -f xml -t order-json.tmpl The SOAP response <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:m="http://example.com/orders"> <soap:Body> <m:GetOrderResponse> <m:Order id="1001"> <m:Customer>Alice Smith</m:Customer> <m:Total currency="EUR">120.50</m:Total> </m:Order> </m:GetOrderResponse> </soap:Body> </soap:Envelope> What bafi sees Namespace prefixes are dropped ( soap:Body is Body ); namespace declarations show up as attributes ( -soap , -m ). Print the parsed structure whenever you are unsure of a path: bafi -i response.xml -t '?{{toJSON .Envelope.Body}}' { "GetOrderResponse": { "Order": { "-id": "1001", "Customer": "Alice Smith", "Total": { "#text": "120.50", "-currency": "EUR" } } } } Template {{- with .Envelope.Body.GetOrderResponse.Order -}} {"id": {{index . "-id"}}, "customer": {{toJSON .Customer}}, "total": {{index .Total "#text"}}, "currency": {{toJSON (index .Total "-currency")}}} {{- end}} cat response.xml | bafi -f xml -t order-json.tmpl {"id": 1001, "customer": "Alice Smith", "total": 120.50, "currency": "EUR"} with sets the dot to the order, so the template does not repeat the long path. If the service can return a SOAP fault instead, test for it with {{if .Envelope.Body.Fault}}...{{end}} . Related: REST response to SOAP request · XML to JSON

docs.text: Query any SQL database into XML or JSON bafi does not connect to databases itself. Combine it with usql , a universal SQL client for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite and more, which prints query results as JSON ( -J ): usql postgres://user:pass@db.example.com/shop -J -q -c "SELECT id, name, email FROM users" \ | bafi -f json -t '?{{toXML .}}' What the query result looks like usql -J prints a JSON array with one object per row: [ {"id": 1, "name": "Alice Smith", "email": "alice@example.com"}, {"id": 2, "name": "Bob Brown", "email": "bob@example.com"} ] Rows to XML cat result.json | bafi -f json -t '?{{toXML .}}' <doc> <record> <email>alice@example.com</email> <id>1</id> <name>Alice Smith</name> </record> <record> <email>bob@example.com</email> <id>2</id> <name>Bob Brown</name> </record> </doc> A top-level array becomes one <record> per row inside <doc> . For your own element names write the XML in a template, as in JSON to XML . The same works with any client that prints JSON or CSV, for example psql --csv (then -f csv ) or sqlite3 -json . Related: JSON to XML · SQL INSERT statements from CSV

docs.text: Convert XML to CSV Flatten repeating XML records into CSV rows, including values stored in attributes. Sample input This is testdata.xml , shipped with every bafi release: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <TOP_LEVEL description="employeeData"> <DATA_LINE> <Employee ID="0021"></Employee> <Trans_Date>2021-05-21</Trans_Date> <val1>5</val1> <val2>12</val2> <Linked_Text VALUE="Magic Bus Company"></Linked_Text> </DATA_LINE> <DATA_LINE> <Employee ID="0023"></Employee> <Trans_Date>2021-05-23</Trans_Date> <val1>43</val1> <val2>9</val2> <Linked_Text VALUE="Baltimore Grand"></Linked_Text> </DATA_LINE> </TOP_LEVEL> Template Employee,Date,val1,val2,SUM,LinkedText {{- range mustArray .TOP_LEVEL.DATA_LINE}} {{index .Employee "-ID"}},{{dateFormat .Trans_Date "2006-01-02" "02.01.2006"}},{{.val1}},{{.val2}},{{add .val1 .val2}},"{{index .Linked_Text "-VALUE"}}" {{- end}} bafi -i data.xml -t employees-csv.tmpl Employee,Date,val1,val2,SUM,LinkedText 0021,21.05.2021,5,12,17,"Magic Bus Company" 0023,23.05.2021,43,9,52,"Baltimore Grand" index .Employee "-ID" reads the ID attribute; attributes are prefixed with - , and keys with a - need index instead of a dot. mustArray keeps the template working when the file contains only one DATA_LINE . dateFormat converts dates using Go's reference layout ( 2006-01-02 means YYYY-MM-DD). add converts the text values to numbers before adding. Related: XML to JSON · JSON to CSV

docs.text: Convert XML to JSON Turn an XML file or API response into JSON, either as a straight conversion or reshaped into exactly the JSON structure you need. Sample input <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <orders> <order id="1001" status="paid"> <customer>Alice Smith</customer> <total currency="EUR">120.50</total> </order> <order id="1002" status="open"> <customer>Bob "Bobby" Brown</customer> <total currency="EUR">80.00</total> </order> </orders> One-line conversion bafi -i orders.xml -t '?{{toJSON .}}' { "orders": { "order": [ { "-id": "1001", "-status": "paid", "customer": "Alice Smith", "total": { "#text": "120.50", "-currency": "EUR" } }, { "-id": "1002", "-status": "open", "customer": "Bob \"Bobby\" Brown", "total": { "#text": "80.00", "-currency": "EUR" } } ] } } How XML maps to the data the template sees: Attributes become keys prefixed with - : id="1001" is -id . Text of an element that also has attributes is stored under #text : <total currency="EUR">120.50</total> becomes {"-currency": "EUR", "#text": "120.50"} . Repeated elements become a list; a single element is not a list (see below ). All values are text; XML has no numbers. Reshape into your own JSON Pick the fields you need and give them your own names. toJSON on a single value produces a correctly quoted and escaped JSON string, so names containing quotes stay valid JSON. [ {{- range $i, $o := .orders.order}}{{if $i}},{{end}} {"id": {{index $o "-id"}}, "customer": {{toJSON $o.customer}}, "total": {{index $o.total "#text"}}, "paid": {{eq (index $o "-status") "paid"}}} {{- end}} ] bafi -i orders.xml -t orders-json.tmpl [ {"id": 1001, "customer": "Alice Smith", "total": 120.50, "paid": true}, {"id": 1002, "customer": "Bob \"Bobby\" Brown", "total": 80.00, "paid": false} ] One element or many If the XML contains a single <order> , .orders.order is that order itself, not a list, and range iterates over its fields instead. Wrap it with mustArray , which turns a single value into a one-item list and leaves lists alone: <orders> <order id="1001"><customer>Alice Smith</customer></order> </orders> bafi -i single.xml -t '?{{range mustArray .orders.order}}{{.customer}}{{end}}' Alice Smith From an API curl -fs https://example.com/api/orders.xml | bafi -f xml -t orders-json.tmpl -o orders.json -f xml is needed because stdin has no file extension. curl -f makes curl fail on HTTP errors instead of piping an error page into bafi. Related: JSON to XML · XML to CSV · SOAP response to JSON
